messages.author: 359edd00939cafec
messages.subject: ctmm::meta() with scaled Homerange-sizes
parts:
Dear all,

I am comparing AKDE sizes using ctmm::meta(). I have two different species and two different treatments. I would like to show that the treatment is the more important predictor of homerange size, although both species slightly differ in their homerange sizes (not significant, and not meaningful). What I did until here:

1) compared both species without considering treatment 
2) compared only treatments
3) compared each species with both treatments

 However, I would like to bring this together and end up with only one estimate of the effect size, how the treatment affects homerange size. I was thinking about scaling (scale()) the homerange sizes for each group and then applying the meta-analysis on these scaled hr estimates. Does that make any sense? I struggle to get my head around the functions within the meta-function, so if anyone has an idea of how to implement it, I would be very happy to learn from you.

Thanks in advance,

Marius

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: ctmm::meta() with scaled Homerange-sizes
parts:
Hi Marius,

You can export the log(home-range area) estimates and their uncertainties with the Log() function and then do more general regressions in the metafor package. At some point, I will have the capabilities for fixed effects in ctmm::meta(), but it's not at the top of the list right now.

Best,
Chris
